description: I am Mohd Owais, a solo AI/ML developer competing as team Space-Max 0. I am building an end-to-end interactive web tool for NASA's SPHEREx mission to detect moving celestial objects and brown dwarfs. I am independently engineering the complete pipeline—from the backend data streaming and infrared spectral ML models to the frontend UI utilising Aladin Lite and Astropy for coordinate mapping.
summary:
Space-Max 0: Orbital Intelligence Engine is a public-facing, cloud-native infrared sky observatory and AI discovery platform built for the "Planet X and SPHEREx" challenge. While NASA’s SPHEREx mission maps the entire sky across 102 near-infrared spectral bands (0.75–5.00 µm), spotting faint, ultra-cold Brown Dwarfs (~250 K) and distant Planet X candidates (~55 K) amidst millions of stars and zodiacal dust glow requires specialized tooling. 

With Space-Max 0, anyone can enter Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) sky coordinates—or select one-click NASA presets—to watch a 6-epoch time-lapse video of that sky patch from the year 2000 (2MASS/WISE) to 2025+ (SPHEREx), making moving celestial objects effortless to spot and lock. Users can slice a 3D WebGL hyperspectral light cube to inspect water (1.4 µm) and methane (3.3 µm) clouds, verify candidates via a PyTorch Tri-Model pipeline (2D-CNN, Spectral RNN, Kinematic GNN) and CSA NEOSSat asteroid vetting, and submit citizen-science RLHF votes.
details:
====================================================================

LIVE LINKS & OPEN-SOURCE DELIVERABLES

====================================================================

• Live Interactive Web Observatory: https://space-max.ai.studio

• Full-Stack Source Code (GitHub): https://github.com/Aluro7in/Space-Max-0

====================================================================

1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

====================================================================

Space-Max 0 transforms raw multi-epoch infrared space telescope telemetry into an intuitive, zero-scroll web observatory that allows scientists, students, and everyday citizen explorers to hunt for moving deep-space anomalies (such as ultra-cold Y/T-class Brown Dwarfs and hypothetical Planet X candidates) across NASA's SPHEREx survey:

• Step 1 — Coordinate Search & 6-Epoch Sky Time-Lapse Video: Users enter any Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates (in decimal degrees or HMS/DMS) or select calibrated NASA target presets (SPHEREx QR2 Candidate, WISE 0855, Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, R Draconis). Space-Max 0 streams real multi-epoch infrared cutouts (Epoch 2000 2MASS, Epoch 2010 AllWISE, and 2025+ SPHEREx passes) and plays them as an interactive 6-frame time-lapse video with breadcrumb motion trails, differential photometry ("Subtract: Now − Past" dipole cancellation), and an interactive golden proper-motion vector overlay (measuring mas/yr and arcsecond displacement).

• Step 2 — 3D WebGL Hyperspectral Light Cube & 102-Band Rainbow Fingerprint: Because SPHEREx captures 102 spectral channels from 0.75 µm to 5.00 µm, Space-Max 0 renders an interactive Three.js 3D volumetric Integral Field Unit (IFU) data cube. Users can rotate the 3D volume and drag the wavelength slicer across all 102 bands to visually inspect molecular absorption troughs for Water Vapor (H2O at 1.4 µm & 1.9 µm), Methane (CH4 at 2.3 µm & 3.3 µm), and Carbon Monoxide (CO at 4.6 µm), while accounting for the SPHEREx 2.42 µm dichroic beam-splitter gap (BLANKCH channels 51–52).

• Step 3 — Tri-Model PyTorch Verification, CSA NEOSSat Vetting & Live Citizen RLHF: Every scan is evaluated by a three-stage PyTorch neural pipeline, vetted against optical star maps (ESA Gaia DR3) and inner-solar-system asteroid archives (Canadian Space Agency NEOSSat / CADC & IMCCE SkyBoT), explained in plain English by the Gemini AI Space Guide, and opened to citizen-science voting with live online Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF).

====================================================================

2. SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

====================================================================

• Radiative Calibration & Astrometry: Raw FITS arrays streamed from AWS S3 (s3://nasa-irsa-spherex/) and NASA IRSA / CDS HiPS2FITS undergo Zodiacal foreground dust subtraction (ZODI), 6-detector median cosmic-ray rejection, and Astropy ZScale percentile clipping paired with an inverse hyperbolic sine stretch:

I(x,y) = asinh( α * [F_raw(x,y) - F_ZODI - B_med] / [P_99.5 - B_med] ) / asinh(α)

Sub-pixel centroiding via DAOStarFinder and 2D Moffat PSF fitting extracts the proper-motion vector μ (mas/yr) and heliocentric kinematic distance regime.

• PyTorch Tri-Model Neural Pipeline + k-NN Spectral Matcher:

1. 2D-CNN (PlanetX_CNN): Classifies 32x32 multi-epoch cutouts to reject hot pixels, diffraction ghosts, and detector artifacts.

2. 102-Band Spectral RNN (LSTM/GRU) & Cosine-Similarity k-NN Matcher: Matches the target's 102-band infrared spectrum against calibrated reference templates (Y2 Ultra-Cool Dwarf ~250 K, T8 Methane Dwarf ~750 K, L4 Dwarf ~1700 K, M8V Red Dwarf ~2700 K, and ~55 K Planet X Methane-Albedo models) to estimate effective temperature (T_eff).

3. Kinematic GNN (Graph Neural Network): Evaluates local star-field proper-motion graphs against ESA Gaia DR3 to isolate high-proper-motion sub-stellar outliers.

• Online PyTorch RLHF Backpropagation & SQLite Persistence: When a citizen scientist clicks "Yes! I Found Planet X", "Camera Glitch", or "Normal Star", the FastAPI backend records the vote in a persistent SQLite database (spacemax_rlhf.db) and executes a live PyTorch gradient step (loss.backward(), optimizer.step()), returning the updated checkpoint version, binary cross-entropy loss, and confidence shift in real time.

====================================================================

3. BENEFITS, INTENDED IMPACT & CREATIVITY

====================================================================

• Democratizing Infrared Astrophysics: Raw Multi-Extension FITS files and 102-channel spectral arrays are inaccessible to the general public. Space-Max 0 turns complex infrared spectrophotometry into an interactive visual experience with role-adaptive AI explanations (Explorer Mode for kids/students, Astrophysicist Mode, and AI Engineer Mode).

• Eliminating False Positives via Multi-Agency Fusion: By combining NASA infrared surveys (SPHEREx, WISE, 2MASS) with ESA optical astrometry (Gaia DR3) and CSA near-Earth surveillance (NEOSSat CADC), Space-Max 0 ensures that fast-moving inner-solar-system asteroids or satellites are never mistaken for deep-space Planet X candidates.

• Exportable Scientific Dossiers: Users can export timestamped JSON discovery dossiers containing WCS coordinates, 102-band spectral flux arrays, PyTorch tri-model logits, and RLHF checkpoint metadata for follow-up telescope observations.

====================================================================

4. TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED

====================================================================

• Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (WebGL 3D volumetric rendering & custom shaders), Recharts (102-band spectral visualization), Aladin Lite v3 / CDS HiPS2FITS, Lucide Icons.

• Backend & Scientific Computing: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Uvicorn, PyTorch (2D-CNN, LSTM/RNN, Kinematic GNN, k-NN cosine matcher, online Adam RLHF trainer), Astropy (FITS & WCS), Photutils (DAOStarFinder astrometry), Astroquery (Gaia DR3 & SkyView), Boto3 (unsigned AWS S3 streaming), NumPy, Matplotlib, SQLite3, OpenGl.

• Cloud Infrastructure: Docker, Render Cloud, Google Cloud Run, Google AI Studio.

====================================================================

5. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) TRANSPARENCY DISCLOSURE

====================================================================

In full compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge Super Intelligence (SI) guidelines:

• Runtime AI Copilot (Code & Text): The interactive "Gemini AI Space Guide" inside the web application uses the Google Gemini API to translate live telescope telemetry into plain-English mission briefings.

• Development & Troubleshooting (Code): Large Language Models (Google Gemini / AI Studio) were utilized by solo developer Mohd Owais for full-stack code scaffolding, debugging, and UI/UX layout optimization.

• Audio / Video & Visual Assets: AI voice synthesis and NotebookLM / Gemini tools assisted in generating the video narration and custom non-NASA mission patch graphic (which is explicitly labeled and contains zero NASA logos or restricted identifiers). All astronomical FITS processing, astrometric calculations, and PyTorch neural network operations execute natively in Python and TypeScript.
